author: NorthEast News Desk
body: FIFA President Gianni Infantino appears to have enough support to win reelection next year, prompting opponents to shift their attention toward reducing presidential power and strengthening governance controls, according to Reuters interviews with people familiar with the discussions.

Infantino faced the most serious challenge of his decade in office after a proposal to sell a 20% stake in FIFA competitions collapsed in July. UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation and CONCACAF opposed the plan, while several European national federations withdrew their support.

Reuters reported that Infantino retains strong relationships with many smaller national associations and support across Oceania, Africa and South America. No viable challenger has emerged before the November 18 nomination deadline, and potential candidates cited in football circles have declined to run.

Opponents are therefore considering a campaign for structural changes, including greater transparency and stronger checks on major commercial decisions. Infantino is seeking another term in the March 18, 2027, election in Rabat. The assessment of his support is based on Reuters sourcing rather than a completed vote; national associations will make the formal decision at the election.
dek: Reuters sources say the FIFA president retains enough association support to survive the challenge, pushing critics to focus on checks on executive power.
headline: Infantino opponents shift toward FIFA governance reform as challenge falters
